post.caption: This gem has two different hardnesses. It is kyanite, named from the Greek word for blue. Along its long axis, hardness is about 4 to 4.5, and across that axis, it is about 6 to 7. Sources vary a little, so treat those numbers as close estimates. Its old name, disthene, means double strength in Greek. It is mostly blue, but also comes in green and orange, and orange kyanite from Tanzania gets its color from manganese. Its perfect cleavage and varied hardness make it hard to cut. Earrings and pendants suit it, while rings need protective settings.
